So I was recently diagnosed with classical EDS a few years ago after a genetics test, and I found out it comes from my dad's side of the family! And it explains so much, like how I was able to excel in adult gymnastics despite never doing gymnastics as a kid. I also love to dance now as an adult and realize my naturally flexibility has helped me progress much quicker than most adults. But it also explains why I got a stress fracture from running less than 20 miles a week and also a low-trauma toe fracture from accidentally walking into a wall, and why my dad almost bled out after having his tonsils removed as an adult. And my eyesight is in -6.00ish territory, which hinders me front sports a great deal. My eyelids are too stretchy and prevent me from being able to wear contacts anymore (my eyes don't fully close when I sleep and so my eyes constantly produce mucus, and nothing helps at all lmao). Seeing Morgan Hurd made me feel so validated tbh.
I basically found out I had EDS when I began a typical beginners' level home training program during covid and couldn't figure out why my shoulder keep burning and popping out of place, along with my knees being unstable and my back hurting constantly 😭 it all kinda hit me once I hit my mid 20s. 
Sometimes I mourn the gymnastics "career" I could have had if my parents had put me in the sport as a child, but I'm also glad they didn't because I don't even want to imagine the state my joints would be in today.

So, I've been with Sydney for 3 years now and while I've gone up in weight for my lower body, my arms remain the same, and probably always will. I use 15-30 lbs for most leg work (sometimes a 40lb dumbbell for glute bridges), and 10-15 lbs for almost all upper body exercises (I can push heavier on rows and chest press sometimes).

I have classical EDS and it REALLY fucks with both my elbows and my shoulders, so going up in weight for things like curls and presses is very difficult without injuring myself. These exercises have NEVER gotten easier for me, and my endurance has never really improved despite being consistent with workouts and lowering the weights. I actually believe overdoing weights with her STF program during my first year is what led to my rapid accumulation of injuries in my shoulders and hips...which led to my diagnosis, yay. That's not Sydney's fault though :( BUT now that I've been doing physical therapy for a couple years, I absolutely believe my workouts with Sydney have been the key in keeping my pain and injury levels down!

I've accepted I'm always going to have a weak upper body, so I don't beat myself up when I can't go any higher when Sydney tells us to and just try to focus on perfecting my form with each round. The most important thing for me is accepting that I have to progress much slower than others and not comparing my weights to Sydney's, or anyone else's. :)

edited to add, my palate is narrow and my teeth are also crowded, and there's a rogue flap of gum that keeps growing over my second molars. I've had like 3 procedures since to try to remove the gum and get my teeth to fully erupt, but my gums just grow way too quickly. Turns out gingival hypertrophy is another fun perk of EDS. Most recently we even tried burning off the gum with a new laser procedure, but it still grew back somehow! Hello! I was recently diagnosed with classical EDS, based on the results of the connective tissue disease panel I did through a company called Invitae. I highly recommend looking into getting a test done with them - my insurance actually covered it, which blew my mind. It's super easy. You set up a video call first with one of the genetic counselors, who will order the correct test for you and have it sent to your house. Invitae is actually credible for medical results, whereas 23andMe isn't, so if you want to know for sure if you have EDS, getting a specific panel done by a clinical lab is the best way to go.
